answer: Rank identities with SybilRank-style random walks. From a few dozen long-standing seed agents, the ledger spreads trust along the attestation graph for only about log(n) steps, then divides each key's score by its degree. Sybils can endorse each other freely, but few edges link them to honest agents, so little trust leaks in before the walk stops, like a drop of pigment barely tinting the next jar. A thousand fake keys, all written by one quill, share that trickle. Seeds are redrawn at each epoch's dawn, so no one can target them.
